clue.text: The Case of the Embassy Official

definitions.meaning: a slim document briefcase named after diplomats who carried one
a staff member ... to an ambassador's mission

explanation.surface: The title of a detective story about a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a Sherlock Holmes title; 'The' and 'of the' are joining words between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché case is a slim briefcase, and an attaché is a junior diplomat posted to a foreign mission.

clue.text: An orchestra providing accompaniment

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A
LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: An orchestra backing a soloist.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes as well, in addition, goes along with the rest as accompaniment.

clue.text: Fashion certain to be that of a monk?

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or high style
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A question of whether a certain look suits a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk traditionally shaves a bare patch on the crown, so the haircut is the fashion belonging to a monk.

clue.text: One vessel destroyed as another is launched?

definitions.text: One vessel destroyed as another is launched?

parts.words: One vessel destroyed as another is launched?
parts.note: at a ship's launch a bottle of fizz is smashed against the hull: one vessel (the bottle) breaks as another vessel (the ship) goes into the water

explanation.surface: A naval disaster at a ship launch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships are traditionally christened by breaking a bottle of sparkling wine on the bow as they slide into the water.

clue.text: Mother topped up the mother of all musicals?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
topped means the head letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: mother as an adjective (mother tongue, mother country) means native

explanation.surface: A mother refilling the greatest stage show of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' leaves ATIVE from NATIVE, and 'up' turns it round. The musical is about Eva Perón, revered as the mother of Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lloyd Webber show tells of Eva Perón, called a spiritual mother of her nation, so its subject is a mother among musicals.

clue.text: Piece of embroiderer's work, first of stitches larger?

indicators.note: first of picks only the opening letter of the word stitches

parts.note: ampler means larger or more generous

explanation.surface: An embroiderer wondering whether to make the opening stitches bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitched panel showing letters and patterns is a traditional embroidery showpiece.

clue.text: Fabric to weave etc, so knit!

indicators.note: weave tells us to interlace these letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An impatient instruction to a textile worker: weave and so on, or else knit.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockinet is a stretchy machine-knitted cloth used for bandages and underwear.

clue.text: I'm easily upset supporting male Shakespearean

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed beneath the other piece

parts.note: someone easily upset could say 'I stress quickly'

explanation.surface: A nervous person explaining that they back men.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'I'm easily upset' is reworded as I STRESS QUICKLY; 'upset' is not an anagram signal. The character is the hostess of the Boar's Head tavern in Henry IV and Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shakespearean character is a figure from his plays, and this tavern hostess appears in several.

clue.text: State briefly unconscious, given wash

parts.note: LA is the short form of the US state Louisiana
under means anaesthetised, unconscious

explanation.surface: A patient briefly knocked out and then given a wash.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder clothes is to wash them.

clue.text: Plant masseuse on top of actor

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top of puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a masseuse rubs people, so is a rubber
Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A masseuse planted on top of an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: The rubber tree is a latex-yielding plant, also kept as a houseplant.

clue.text: Republic of unsettled Romanians

indicators.note: unsettled suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A state populated by restless Romanians.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent republic surrounded by Italy.

clue.text: Young flier last to confess, being British

indicators.note: last to takes only the final letter of the word confess

parts.note: qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of being

explanation.surface: A youngster, being British, the last to own up.
explanation.definitionFit: A squab is a young pigeon not yet fledged, a bird that will fly.

clue.text: Carry over subject of contract, getting rise on the way

parts.note: to hump something is to carry it with effort
back means over, as in a thing done and gone
contract bridge is the card game, so bridge is what contract describes

explanation.surface: Legal-sounding talk of carrying over a contract's subject and getting a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject of contract' sounds legal; it is the card game contract bridge. The definition describes a sharply arched road bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeply arched bridge makes the road climb in a bump, a rise along the route.

clue.text: Sport for which I can get ski modified

indicators.note: modified tells us to change the order of these letters

explanation.surface: A sport someone can take up with skis adapted for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gliding on blades over a frozen rink is a winter sport.

clue.text: Exercise by the right breaks decent minister

indicators.note: breaks means the pieces burst into the middle of the other word

parts.note: clean means decent, wholesome
R is the abbreviation for right
gym is exercise, as in a PE class

explanation.surface: A workout routine involving a decent minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman is a minister of the church.

clue.text: Potter: Punk singer making comeback, unhip

parts.note: Punk is the setter, so his name stands for me

indicators.note: making comeback, in a down clue, means this word is read upwards

parts.note: a bass is a low-voiced singer
out means out of fashion, unhip

explanation.surface: A punk rock singer staging a return, no longer cool.
explanation.walkthrough: Punk is the setter's pseudonym, so it gives ME; 'making comeback' turns BASS to SSAB. 'Potter' is a verb, to dawdle aimlessly, not Harry or Beatrix.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to fiddle around doing small idle tasks, to fool around aimlessly.

clue.text: Row round river to see fish

indicators.note: round means the first word goes around the other

parts.note: a spat is a row, a quarrel

explanation.surface: Rowing round a river to spot fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small herring-like sea fish.

clue.text: Black is black in transaction

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sale is a commercial transaction
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A remark about a business deal done on the black market.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic and poetic word for the colour black.

clue.text: More like seawater in flooding heath

indicators.note: flooding means the little word pours into the middle of the other

parts.note: brier, or briar, is the heath plant whose root makes pipes

explanation.surface: Salty water flooding a heath.
explanation.definitionFit: Brine is salt water, so something brinier is saltier, closer to the sea.

clue.text: Fixed old-fashioned technical drawing instrument

parts.note: set means fixed, settled
square is slang for staid and old-fashioned

explanation.surface: A dated drawing tool that has been repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangular plate used to draw right angles is a draughtsman's tool.

clue.text: Longing to get at controversial artist?

parts.note: Damien Hirst is the artist famous for a pickled shark

explanation.surface: Wanting to get at a provocative artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Being athirst is craving or eager for something, as if thirsty.

clue.text: One leading to ruin in the clutches of an intelligent, sexy woman?

indicators.note: in the clutches of means held tight inside the other piece

parts.note: bright means intelligent, so an intelligent gives a bright
I is the Roman numeral for one
to fall is what something leading to ruin results in

explanation.surface: A man ruined by a clever seductive woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the clutches of' wraps A BRIGHT around I and TO FALL. The phrase is British slang for an attractive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone this is British slang for finding them very attractive.

clue.text: Flower for all to see, something to draw around

indicators.note: around means the first word wraps the other

parts.note: lots are drawn to decide something at random
U is the British film rating for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A flower displayed publicly, something to sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film classification meaning suitable for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily-like flower sacred in Asian religions.

clue.text: Druggie queen of republic?

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States, a republic
ER is the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A monarch of a republic who takes drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug user is someone who takes illegal substances.

clue.text: Silly person gives bad African good books

parts.note: Idi Amin was the brutal Ugandan dictator
OT is the Old Testament, the books of the Good Book

explanation.surface: A foolish person handing out awful African literature.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a fool.

clue.text: Dismissed opener for Surrey, short hit going the wrong way, getting edge

parts.note: out means dismissed, as a batter in cricket

indicators.note: opener for takes the first letter of Surrey
going the wrong way means the trimmed word is read backwards
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a strike is a hit or blow

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a Surrey opening batter out to a mishit edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts STRIKE to STRIK, and 'going the wrong way' turns it to KIRTS. Surrey is an English county cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer fringes of a town are its edge.

clue.text: Man pocketing contents of sleeve in coat, perhaps

indicators.note: pocketing means the first word takes the other inside it

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a man
an arm is what fills a sleeve

explanation.surface: A man with his arm in his coat sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat is one example of an item of clothing.

clue.text: Disreputable type first to stop female operation, half finished

indicators.note: first to takes the opening letter of the word stop
half finished means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: a hysterectomy is surgery to remove the womb

explanation.surface: A rogue who halts a gynaecological operation midway.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is an unscrupulous professional, especially a crooked lawyer.
